title: Interview utilities: bind, once, memoize, and flatten
hook: FAANG JavaScript rounds still ask you to implement Function.prototype.bind, once, memoize, or flatten from scratch — each tests closures, this binding, argument forwarding, and edge cases like circular arrays.

blocks.text: **bind**: return wrapper fixing `this` and partial args. **once**: call fn at most one time, cache result. **memoize**: cache by args key. **flatten**: reduce nested arrays to depth N; handle sparse arrays and non-array elements. Know **[[Call]]** semantics: bound function has special `this` behavior.

entries.plainDefinition: Create function with fixed this and prepended args.
Execute original only first call; return cached value.
Nested array to flat to depth.

blocks.text: These utilities appear in lodash source reading and framework internals. bind explains arrow vs function this. flatten with depth mirrors Array.prototype.flat. Production: once for singleton init; memoize bounded for parse functions.

blocks.title: polyfill vs production
blocks.body: Interview: implement bind without calling native bind — use apply + closure.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: bind without apply. once not caching throw. flatten infinite on circular array without guard.

blocks.text: Follow-ups: debounce, throttle, curry, promiseAll limit. lodash implementations for comparison. TypeScript generic typings for memoize. bind + new: FBound extends bound function prototype.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Cannot implement bind. once calls fn every time. flatten only one level always.

interviewTakeaways: 60s: bind fixes this via apply wrapper. once caches first result. memoize Map bounded. flatten recursive depth. Arrow bind no-op on this.
commonPitfalls: Strong: apply-based bind + once + flatten depth + arrow caveat.
